interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 3+4 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 2) and pathological stage pT3b. Adverse findings include positive surgical margins, invasion of the seminal vesicles, lymphovascular invasion, and lymph node metastasis. The biopsy findings showed Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) with cribriform pattern and perineural invasion. Countervailing findings are not documented. The nodal status is documented as lymph node metastasis was present. Missing postoperative PSA prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. The documented pathology indicates a high-risk disease profile. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. The current findings suggest a high risk, and the trajectory of postoperative PSA will be a key factor in determining subsequent management. The fixed estimated horizon is 27.33 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 20.49–34.16 months; its coverage has not been validated.
